==Latin==
{{was fwotd|la|2018|May|15}}

===Etymology===
{{root|la|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}}
{{ety|la|:inh|itc-pro:*fameliā}}
From {{inh|la|itc-pro|*fameliā||of the house → household}}, from earlier ''*θameliā''. Further from {{inh|la|ine-pro|*dʰh₁-m-eló-m||fundament}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-||to do, put, place}}. Cognate with {{cog|sa|धामन्||order; dwelling-place, temple; family}}, {{cog|grc|θεμέλιος||of the foundation}}, {{m|grc|θέμις||justice, law}}.<ref>{{R:itc:EDL|page=200|head=famulus|passage=Derivatives > line 2 > ''familia''}}</ref>

In view of the semantic shift illustrated in the cognates, {{m|la|famulus||servant, slave}} (with {{cog|osc|𐌚𐌀𐌌𐌄𐌋||servile}}) is probably a backformation from it and not the other way around.

===Pronunciation===
* {{la-IPA}}

===Noun===
{{la-noun|familia<1>|gen_sg=familiae/familiās}}

# a [[household]] {{gloss|all [[persons]] subject to the control of one man (whether [[relation]]s, [[freedman|freedmen]] or [[slave]]s)}}
# the [[slaves]] of a household, [[servants]]
# a [[group]] of slaves stationed in one place; a [[brigade]], [[gang]] (used for some purpose)
## one's personal [[retinue]]
# a [[family]], [[kin]] {{gloss|a group of people closely related to one another}}
#: {{syn|la|domus}}
#* {{Q|la|Vulgate|Genesis|10|32|quote=Hae '''familiae''' Nōē iū̆xtā populōs et nātiōnēs suās. Ab hīs dīvīsae sunt gentēs in Terrā post dīluvium.|t=These are the '''families''' of Noah, according to their peoples and tribes. From them split the nations on Earth after the deluge.}}<!--nātiō is usually smaller than gēns-->
# an intellectual [[school]] (e.g., of philosophy)
#: {{syn|la|domus}}
# {{lb|la|law}} an [[estate]] (sometimes distinct from {{m|la|pecūnia}} and possibly restricted to {{m|la|rēs mancipī}})

====Usage notes====
According to Richard Saller, “''[f]amilia'' was never used to mean ‘father, mother and children’ in our sense of ‘family’ today. It did have a technical, legal usage akin to ‘family’, but in common parlance most often meant ‘slave staff’, exclusive of the master's family.... The usual word for ‘family’ in the classical period was {{m|la|domus}}, which carried the general sense of ‘household’ including domestic slaves.”<ref>Saller, Richard, ''Slavery and the Roman Family'', in Finley, Moses I., ed., ''Classical Slavery'' (London: Frank Cass, cloth 1987 & 2000 (same ed.), reprinted 1999 {{ISBN|0-7146-3320-8}}, p.&nbsp;84</ref>

{{la-ndecl|familia<1>|gen_sg=familiae/familiās|footnote=The Old Latin genitive singular {{m|la|familiās}} is used in {{m|la|pater familiās}} and similar expressions with {{m|la|fīlius}}, {{m|la|māter}}, and {{m|la|fīlia}} as the first element.}}
